purpose: Test whether matching SDXL identity-LoRA training resolution to the final full-body ControlNet frame resolves the identity-versus-structure failure.
dataset: 19 approved full-body reference views; no scene images, face crops, or hand-detail images

heldout.prompt_contract: cinema foyer at night, low side three-quarter full body, left hand picks up ticket

assessment.0.0: Identity-only baseline retained teal bob, white jacket, teal trousers, white sneakers, and navy bag, but did not perform the low bent ticket action.
assessment.0.1: Retained most identity cues and changed the background perspective, but the full-body pose remained upright; no useful ticket action control.
assessment.0.35: Restored the bent pose and diagonal foyer perspective, but inverted the jacket and trouser color/structure and changed the bag.
assessment.0.75: Strengthened the bent pose and camera structure, while identity drift remained: teal jacket, white trousers, and a different bag.
assessment.conclusion: Native full-body training resolution is feasible on 8 GB and improves the LoRA-only reference appearance, but it does not create an acceptable Canny scale where both identity and dynamic structure pass. Do not add inpaint or another condition to this branch.

retention: The final scale contact sheet, record, and two source scripts are retained. The high-resolution LoRA adapter, materialized dataset, and individual per-scale sheets were removed after review.
